Issued at 225 PM CDT Fri Oct 16 2026

The last of the clouds will continue to diminish over northwest
Iowa and southwest Minnesota over the hour or two, leading to 
plenty of sunshine across the area! This sunshine should allow 
most areas to reach the lower 50s for highs, and decreasingly 
breezy winds will make for a cool, but fairly pleasant fall 
evening. 

Winds will be decreasing due to a surface high pressure
system moving across the region. These lighter winds coupled 
with clear skies will mean temperatures will drop rather quickly
after the sun sets. By the late night hours though, the high 
pressure system will quickly slide eastward and allow for the 
return of southeasterly winds to the area. This should halt the
faster cooling and allow for areas especially over south- 
central South Dakota to remain above freezing, though still 
remain cold enough for frost. Thus, a frost advisory will be in
effect for these areas tonight. Farther east, do think the 
slight uptick in southeasterly winds will not make it in time to
prevent these areas from dropping to 32 degrees or lower. 
Generally speaking, the farther east you go across the area
tonight, the longer it will take for the slightly elevated 
winds to arrive and thus the colder you'll get. Though there is 
still some lingering uncertainty on the westward extent of the 
freezing temperatures, current thoughts are that clear skies, 
light winds, and dry air during the early overnight will lead to 
these areas dropping to freezing by daybreak. All that said, 
frost is expected across the entire area overnight. 

Southeasterly winds will continue to increase heading into the day 
tomorrow as the high pressure system slides east and a low pressure 
system develops off the northern Rockies. Winds won't be as strong 
as what we've seen this morning and this past night, but expect most 
areas to see gusts in the 25-35 mph range during the day on 
Saturday. A few gusts to 45 mph will be possible over the higher 
elevations of the Buffalo Ridge, but this is not expected to be 
widespread enough to warrant wind headlines at this time, though
trends will be monitor. Another thing to monitor will be 
locally elevated fire weather conditions Saturday afternoon. 
Warmer temperatures are expected especially over south-central 
South Dakota, with highs in the 60s and possibly near 70. This 
combined with dew points well down into the 30s will lead to 
relative humidity values just below 30% in south-central South 
Dakota. Elsewhere, relative humidity values will be around 
30-50% Saturday afternoon. This could all result in locally 
elevated fire weather concerns mainly in cured grasses and 
cropland. 

Ridging aloft builds in through the weekend, allowing for a 
seasonal weather pattern to return that will also continue into
early next week. Sunday looks to be the better weekend day for 
outdoor activities with diminishing winds, sunny skies, and 
highs in the middle 60s. A weak upper wave will ride into the 
central Plains into the upper Midwest Tuesday into Tuesday 
night, though probabilities of measurable rainfall with this 
system is low (<20%) and focused near and east of I-29 according
to latest LREF probabilities. After this weak system passes 
through, ridging builds back in aloft, and this combined with 
continued southerly flow will lead to even warmer temperatures 
by the middle of the week. Highs by Wednesday and Thursday will
potentially climb into the 70s across parts of the area. The 
NBM is a bit more aggressive than other ensembles, though is 
only warmer by a few degrees comparatively speaking. Either 
way, forecast temperatures will likely get refined as mid week 
approaches as more smaller scale details come into better focus. 
Looking out to the end of next week, the weather pattern may 
turn a bit more active as guidance indicates a western trough 
potentially ejecting into the area, though the timing of this is
where models really diverge. The broad 20-40% PoPs as 
highlighted by the NBM next Friday is largely in line with 
16.12Z LREF, though details with this system will once again 
become more clear as we approach the end of next week.
